```
code tunnel user login --provider github

The login command stores the selected credential, and tunnel startup is intentionally a separate operation, as documented by the maintainer guidance at https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/207931#issuecomment-2018342545. This avoids the provider-choice prompt, so closing as designed.

Thanks for the report. This is already supported by combining the two switches:

```bash
code \
  --folder-uri "vscode-remote://attached-container+[container-hex]/path-to-project" \
  --goto \

rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the detailed example. If the repository was cloned into a Docker volume, `/workspace` exists inside the Dev Container but not as that path on the Docker daemon host. For these scripts, the available alternatives are baking them into the images, sharing them through a named volume, or using Compose `configs`: https://docs.docker.com/reference/compose-file/configs/

rows.title: Dev Container: /workspaces not user writable
rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the report and discussion. The `/workspaces` parent is expected to remain root-owned because only the mounted workspace folder is preserved across rebuilds; allowing unrelated content there could create an unexpected data-loss risk.

For a writable, persistent `/workspaces` containing sibling projects, configure `workspaceMount` as documented at https://code.visualstudio.com/remote/advancedcontainers/change-default-source-mount, for example: `source=${localWorkspaceFolder}/..,target=/workspaces,type=bind,consistency=cached`.

Reports where the actual mounted workspace folder is not writable under rootless Docker are a separate problem being investigated in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-remote-release/issues/11279.
